# `encoding/json/v2` under `encoding/json` (Go 1.27)

## Thesis

Go 1.27 did not merely *add* `encoding/json/v2`. It also **rewired** the existing `encoding/json` package so that v1 calls run on the v2 engine with a compatibility option set (`DefaultOptionsV1`). Your import paths can stay on v1 forever under the Go 1 compatibility promise; your error *strings* can still change; and the moment you flip an import to `encoding/json/v2`, the **defaults** flip to stricter, more interoperable behaviour. This chapter is the transition guide: what changed even if you never import v2, how to opt in/out, and a side-by-side you can run on Go 1.27+.

It does **not** replace the stdlib survey in `985-encoding-json-csv-xml.qmd` or the performance notes in `261-json-performance-patterns.qmd`. Read those for tags, encoders, and pooling; stay here for the 1.27 semantics shift.

Verified with **Go 1.27.2** (`linux/amd64`) on 2026-10-09. Primary: [Go 1.27 release notes](https://go.dev/doc/go1.27), [json/v2 migration guide](https://go.dev/doc/jsonv2-migration), [`encoding/json` "Migrating to v2"](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json).

## Learning goals

- Explain "v1 API, v2 engine" and when error text can change without an import change  
- Produce identical bytes from `encoding/json/v2` via `json.DefaultOptionsV1()`  
- List the high-impact default differences (nil slice, `omitempty`, case, duplicates, UTF-8, `time.Duration`, HTML escape)  
- Opt out with `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` and know it is temporary  
- Sketch an option-by-option or `jsonsplit` migration for production services  
- Note the adjacent Go 1.27 `net/http` `Response.Body.Close` drain behaviour that bites JSON clients  

## Mental model

```text
Go ≤1.26                         Go 1.27+
────────                         ────────
encoding/json  → old engine      encoding/json  → json/v2 engine
                                      + DefaultOptionsV1 (implicit)

encoding/json/v2 (experiment)    encoding/json/v2  → strict defaults
encoding/json/jsontext           encoding/json/jsontext (tokens)
```

| Knob | Effect |
|------|--------|
| Keep `import "encoding/json"` | Behaviour preserved; error **message text** may differ; faster unmarshal |
| `import jsonv2 "encoding/json/v2"` | New API + **strict defaults** |
| `jsonv2.Marshal(v, json.DefaultOptionsV1())` | v2 API, v1 semantics |
| Later options after `DefaultOptionsV1()` | Override one behaviour at a time |
| `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` at **build** time | Restore pre-1.27 engine behind v1 (escape hatch; expected to vanish) |

`DefaultOptionsV1` (from `encoding/json`) is the full boolean bundle that defines v1 semantics — including `FormatNilMapAsNull`, `OmitEmptyWithLegacySemantics`, `FormatDurationAsNano`, `MatchCaseSensitiveDelimiter`, and friends. Later options win.

## Case 0 — toolchain

```bash
go version
# go version go1.27.2 linux/amd64
```

If you are still on ≤1.26, read this chapter against the published 1.27 notes and upgrade before treating the listings as executable.

## Case 1 — same struct, four marshal paths

```go
// json_transition.go — v1 vs v2 vs Options
package main

import (
	jsonv1 "encoding/json"
	"encoding/json/jsontext"
	jsonv2 "encoding/json/v2"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

type User struct {
	Name    string   `json:"name"`
	Tags    []string `json:"tags"`
	Admin   bool     `json:"admin,omitempty"`
	Retries int      `json:"retries,omitempty"`
}

func show(label string, b []byte, err error) {
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("%-12s ERROR: %v\n", label, err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Printf("%-12s %s\n", label, b)
}

func main() {
	u := User{Name: "ana"} // Tags==nil, Admin==false, Retries==0

	b, err := jsonv1.Marshal(u)
	show("v1", b, err)
	b, err = jsonv2.Marshal(u)
	show("v2", b, err)
	b, err = jsonv2.Marshal(u, jsonv1.DefaultOptionsV1())
	show("v2+OptsV1", b, err)
	b, err = jsonv2.Marshal(u, jsonv1.DefaultOptionsV1(),
		jsonv2.FormatNilSliceAsNull(false))
	show("v2 mix", b, err)

	_ = jsontext.AllowInvalidUTF8 // used below
	_ = time.Second
}
```

```text
v1           {"name":"ana","tags":null}
v2           {"name":"ana","tags":[],"admin":false,"retries":0}
v2+OptsV1    {"name":"ana","tags":null}
v2 mix       {"name":"ana","tags":[]}
```

Three lessons in four lines:

1. **Nil slice:** v1 → JSON `null`; v2 → `[]`.  
2. **`omitempty`:** v1 drops `false` / `0`; v2's `omitempty` drops a field only when it would encode as `null`, `""`, `{}`, or `[]` — so `false` and `0` reappear. Prefer **`omitzero`** on bools/numbers/pointers/interfaces (same meaning in both packages).  
3. **`DefaultOptionsV1` then override** is the supported gradual path (`v2 mix` keeps v1 options except nil-slice formatting).

## Case 2 — unmarshal mismatches that hide in green tests

```go
// continue in main(), after the marshal demos
fmt.Println("== case-insensitive field names ==")
in := []byte(`{"NAME":"bob"}`)
var u1, u2 User
fmt.Printf("v1 name=%q err=%v\n", u1.Name, jsonv1.Unmarshal(in, &u1))
// reset u1 for clarity
u1 = User{}
_ = jsonv1.Unmarshal(in, &u1)
_ = jsonv2.Unmarshal(in, &u2)
fmt.Printf("v1 name=%q\n", u1.Name)
fmt.Printf("v2 name=%q\n", u2.Name)

fmt.Println("== duplicate names ==")
dup := []byte(`{"name":"alice","name":"mallory"}`)
var d1, d2 User
err1 := jsonv1.Unmarshal(dup, &d1)
err2 := jsonv2.Unmarshal(dup, &d2)
fmt.Printf("v1 name=%q err=%v\n", d1.Name, err1)
fmt.Printf("v2 name=%q err=%v\n", d2.Name, err2)

fmt.Println("== invalid UTF-8 ==")
bad := []byte{'{', '"', 'n', 'a', 'm', 'e', '"', ':', '"', 'c', 'a', 'f', 0xff, 'e', '"', '}'}
var x1, x2 User
fmt.Printf("v1 err=%v name=%q\n", jsonv1.Unmarshal(bad, &x1), x1.Name)
fmt.Printf("v2 err=%v\n", jsonv2.Unmarshal(bad, &x2))
fmt.Printf("v2+allow err=%v\n",
	jsonv2.Unmarshal(bad, &x2, jsontext.AllowInvalidUTF8(true)))
```

Actual Go 1.27.2 output:

```text
== case-insensitive field names ==
v1 name="bob"
v2 name=""
== duplicate names ==
v1 name="mallory" err=<nil>
v2 name="alice" err=jsontext: duplicate object member name "name"
== invalid UTF-8 ==
v1 err=<nil> name="caf�e"
v2 err=jsontext: invalid UTF-8 within "/name" after offset 12
v2+allow err=<nil>
```

| Behaviour | v1 default | v2 default | Compatibility lever |
|-----------|------------|------------|---------------------|
| Field name match | Case-insensitive | Case-sensitive | `jsonv2.MatchCaseInsensitiveNames(true)` or tag `case:ignore` |
| Duplicate object names | Last wins | Error | `jsontext.AllowDuplicateNames(true)` |
| Invalid UTF-8 in strings | Replace with U+FFFD | Error | `jsontext.AllowInvalidUTF8(true)` |

**Trap:** after a failed `Unmarshal`, the destination may be partially written (duplicate-name case kept `"alice"`). Discard it.

## Case 3 — `time.Duration` and HTML escaping

```go
type Job struct {
	Name    string        `json:"name"`
	Timeout time.Duration `json:"timeout"`
}
j := Job{Name: "backup", Timeout: 90 * time.Second}
show("v1 dur", jsonv1.Marshal(j))
show("v2 dur", jsonv2.Marshal(j))
show("v2+nano", jsonv2.Marshal(j, jsonv1.FormatDurationAsNano(true)))

type Q struct {
	Q string `json:"q"`
}
q := Q{Q: "<a&b>"}
show("v1 html", jsonv1.Marshal(q))
show("v2 html", jsonv2.Marshal(q))
show("v2+esc", jsonv2.Marshal(q, jsontext.EscapeForHTML(true)))
```

```text
v1 dur       {"name":"backup","timeout":90000000000}
v2 dur       ERROR: json: unable to marshal from Go time.Duration within "/timeout": no default representation
v2+nano      {"name":"backup","timeout":90000000000}
v1 html      {"q":"\u003ca\u0026b\u003e"}
v2 html      {"q":"<a&b>"}
v2+esc       {"q":"\u003ca\u0026b\u003e"}
```

v2 refuses to invent a `Duration` encoding; pass `FormatDurationAsNano(true)` (defined on the v1 package's Options) or change the field type / custom marshaler. HTML escaping is **off** by default in v2 — turn it on if you embed JSON in HTML.

## Portable tags (same bytes under both packages)

```go
type Portable struct {
	Name    string   `json:"name,case:ignore"`
	Tags    []string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
	Admin   bool     `json:"admin,omitzero"`
	Retries int      `json:"retries,omitzero"`
}
```

- `omitempty` on the slice sidesteps `null` vs `[]` by omitting both empty forms.  
- `omitzero` replaces legacy `omitempty` on bool/int.  
- `case:ignore` keeps accepting `"NAME"` under v2.  

Round-trip test idea: `jsonv1.Marshal` and `jsonv2.Marshal` must return identical bytes for your golden structs.

## Migration playbook

1. **Upgrade to 1.27, keep v1 imports.** Fix tests that assert on `err.Error()` strings; assert types (`*json.SyntaxError`, …) instead.  
2. **Optional escape hatch:** `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` while you file upstream issues — not a long-term plan.  
3. **API migration (safe):** switch call sites to `encoding/json/v2` **with** `json.DefaultOptionsV1()`.  
4. **Behaviour migration:** flip one option at a time (`FormatNilSliceAsNull(false)`, …) behind tests.  
5. **Production servers:** consider [`github.com/go-json-experiment/jsonsplit`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-json-experiment/jsonsplit) (`CallBothButReturnV1` + difference reporting) before `OnlyCallV2`.  
6. **New code:** prefer `encoding/json/v2` defaults; use `RejectUnknownMembers(true)` on untrusted request bodies.

Experiment-era blog posts (GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 on 1.25/1.26) may still show removed tag options (`format:`, `unknown:`) or the old `inline` name — 1.27 renamed that to **`embed`** and dropped several experiment-only knobs. Trust `go doc` on 1.27+, not the experiment posts.

## Adjacent Go 1.27 note — `Response.Body.Close` drains

Unrelated to the json packages, but it shows up in the same upgrade window for HTTP+JSON clients: Go 1.27's `net/http` **HTTP/1** `Response.Body` now **drains unread content on `Close`** (up to a conservative limit) to improve connection reuse. For most programs this is a silent win. If you were accidentally leaving huge unread bodies and relying on `MaxIdleConns` quirks, profiles may change — set `Transport.DisableKeepAlives` only if you truly do not want reuse, and prefer reading/decoding the body fully (`json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode` + `Close`) as you already should.

## The trap

- **"We did not import v2, so nothing changed."** The engine underneath v1 did. Golden error strings are the usual breakage.  
- **Trivial import swap without reading defaults.** Nil slices, `omitempty`, and `Duration` are the first production pages.  
- **Keeping partial structs after failed v2 `Unmarshal`.**  
- **Relying on `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` past the migration.** Release notes say it is expected to go away.  
- **Copying experiment-era tags** (`format:`, `inline` instead of `embed`).

## The boring rule

Stay on `encoding/json` until you need v2's API or defaults. When you move, start with `DefaultOptionsV1()`, peel options off under tests, and pin wire contracts with `omitzero` / `case:ignore` / explicit nil-slice policy. Measure unmarshal wins; do not assume marshal is free on every workload.

## Try this

```bash
go install golang.org/dl/go1.27.2@latest   # or use your distro's 1.27
# put the listings in a module with `go 1.27` and `go run .`
GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2 go test ./...       # compare only while diagnosing
```
